title: [PATCH v17 03/18] EDAC: Add ECS control feature (Linux kernel mailing list)
supports: DDR5 ECS (JESD79-5) lets the DRAM internally read, correct single-bit errors and write back; it counts codewords with errors (codeword mode) or rows with errors (row mode); counts below a per-Gbit threshold of 256, 1024 or 4096 are masked (via search snippet; resp-raw-ber-contract WebSearch 1/3). Used for: per-die singleton (pre-correction) counts on DDR5 as the raw-BER leg answering RT-DEV-02 / RT-PROC-01 / RT-IND-04.

title: Linux sysfs-edac-ecs ABI documentation
supports: ECS control is exposed by the Linux EDAC bus (ecs_fruX), including for CXL memory devices (via search snippet; WebSearch 1/3). Whether the count register reports pre-correction errors at bit resolution is NOT confirmed by the search.

title: US 12,430,203 (ECS error counter loaded to a register after a full-die scrub)
supports: One vendor design: the ECS error counter result is loaded into a register after every row of every bank has been scrubbed (via search snippet; WebSearch 1/3). Treated as one design, not the standard.

title: DDR5 SDRAM (Wikipedia)
supports: DDR5 cut the refresh window from 64 ms to 32 ms up to 85 C (16 ms at 85-95 C); tRFC4 retired; tRFCsb (same-bank refresh) added (via search snippet; WebSearch 2/3). Used for: the model's DDR5 baseline correction (tREFI 3.9 us x 8192 = 32 ms) and the DDR5 retention-tail derate.

title: DDR5 specification excerpt (course copy)
supports: Refresh 32 ms / 16 ms with 8192 refresh cycles; per-density cycle times deferred to die-revision datasheets (via search snippet; WebSearch 2/3). The search did NOT confirm a 64Gb tRFC or the 410 ns 32Gb value.

title: antmicro/ddr5-tester: open FPGA platform for RDIMM DDR5
supports: Apache-2.0 KiCad design of an FPGA test platform for DDR5 RDIMMs; Rev 2.x uses an AMD Artix UltraScale+ FPGA and works with the open Rowhammer Tester (via search snippet; WebSearch 3/3). Used for: the DDR5 leg of the revised decisive experiment.

title: Supporting Rowhammer research to protect the DRAM ecosystem (Google)
supports: Google funded Antmicro's open FPGA DDR5 RDIMM and SO-DIMM test platforms; used with ETH Zurich for 'Phoenix' (DDR5 TRR reverse-engineering, IEEE S&P 2026) (via search snippet; WebSearch 3/3). Shows DDR5 command-level testing is feasible on open hardware.

title: Versatile SO-DIMM (LP)DDR5 Rowhammer testing platform
supports: Follow-up Antmicro board supports DDR5 SO-DIMM and an LPDDR5 testbed, with PCIe (via search snippet; WebSearch 3/3).
